comments.body: **Verbatim copy risks future drift from the live document** `OUTPUT_F_UPDATED_DOCUMENTS/docs/architecture/OVERVIEW.md` is a byte-for-byte snapshot of `docs/architecture/OVERVIEW.md` as committed in this PR. If `docs/architecture/OVERVIEW.md` is subsequently revised, the archived copy in this audit record will silently diverge and could mislead anyone using the audit folder as a historical reference. Consider adding a brief header note to this file making it clear this is a point-in-time snapshot: ```suggestion # T81 Architecture Overview ```

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Update expected labels for sequential mesh reflection**

These assertions assume each monad reflects against a snapshot of pre-round labels, but `MeshReflector::mesh_reflect` mutates `monads` in-place as it iterates, so the second monad reads the first monad’s already-updated label in the same round. As written, this assertion (and the later second-round label assertions) will fail whenever assertions are enabled (for example in local debug/assert builds), causing `t81_tier6_test` to abort even though the implementation behavior is unchanged.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**In-place mutation causes synchronous-round test to fail** `mesh_reflect()` in `distributed_monad.cpp` mutates each monad's `label` **in-place** during the single `for (auto& m : monads)` loop. This means that when `monads[1]` (m2) is processed, the peer lookup for m1 returns the **already-updated** value `"node1+node2"` rather than the original `"node1"`. Tracing the first call: | Step | monad | composite built from | result label | |------|-------|----------------------|--------------| | 1 | m1 | `"node1"` + peer m2 (`"node2"`) | `"node1+node2"` ✓ written to `monads[0]` | | 2 | m2 | `"node2"` + peer m1 (**now** `"node1+node2"`) | `"node2+node1+node2"` ✗ | So the assertion on line 43 `assert(monads[1].label == "node2+node1")` will fail at runtime; the actual value is `"node2+node1+node2"`. All subsequent assertions in this test (lines 50–51) are also invalidated. The test correctly encodes the intended **synchronous (Jacobi)** semantics — each monad should see the *pre-round* labels of its peers. The implementation needs to snapshot all labels before the loop. This is a bug in the existing `experimental/tiers/cog/tier6/distributed_monad.cpp` that this PR needs to fix before the tests can pass.

**Redundant `t81_tracing` link dependency** `t81_tracing` is declared as an `OBJECT` library (line 195) and its objects are already compiled directly into `t81_core` via `target_sources(t81_core PRIVATE $)` (line 202). Listing it again here is redundant — the symbols are already present through `t81_core`. Compare with the analogous `t81_tier5_test` target which links only `t81_core t81_experimental`. ```suggestion target_link_libraries(t81_tier6_test PRIVATE t81_core t81_experimental) ```

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Preserve structured policy-denial evidence for Arm A**

For an over-limit purchase such as quantity 100 and unit price 1000, `experiments/architecture_challenge/arm_a.cpp` exits successfully with `status: "denied"`, but this check now raises before `submit_transaction` can return `POLICY_LIMIT_EXCEEDED` and before `execute_runner` writes any evidence. Arm B still returns the structured denial for the same input, so ordinary policy rejection now aborts Arm A experiments instead of producing comparable rejection evidence. Handle native policy denials separately from runtime failures and preserve the runner's denial envelope.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Use an actual delimiter collision in the HMAC regression test**

The shifted authority value has an extra leading colon: the original fields encode as `tx:1:v2`, whereas these substituted fields encode as `tx::1:v2`. Consequently, the previous vulnerable colon-delimited implementation also passes this new regression test, so it does not protect against reintroducing the boundary-shifting vulnerability. Use `authority_version="1:v2"` with `tx_id="tx"` so the two inputs collide under the old encoding but produce different canonical-JSON signatures.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Make the result classifications mutually exclusive**

When the candidate meets the instruction, misprediction, and significance thresholds but is no faster than baseline 2, the same run is both VALIDATED and FALSIFIED. For example, instruction means of 80 versus 100, mispredictions of 5 versus 10, p = 0.001, and latencies of 110 versus 100 satisfy both predicates. INCONCLUSIVE also overlaps FALSIFIED through the latency condition. Resolve whether baseline-2 latency is a prerequisite or a secondary outcome and encode disjoint predicates before freezing the protocol; otherwise identical measurements permit contradictory research dispositions. AGENTS.md requires an explicit falsifier and measurement plan for new experiments.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Preserve inconclusive outcomes in the falsification criterion**

Under this rule, even an underpowered or noisy run that fails to reject the null must be recorded as falsifying packed-ternary performance advantages for pattern filtering generally. **<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Bound evaluation points to exclude polynomial degeneracy**

The proposed domain permits evaluation points that defeat the replacement workload's stated computational depth: x=1 reduces evaluation to the same coefficient sum criticized earlier, x=−1 gives an alternating sum, and x=0 returns only c₀. More broadly, for every even x, xⁱ vanishes modulo 2⁶⁴ once i≥64, so an optimized evaluator can ignore almost the entire high-degree polynomial. Specify the evaluation-point distribution and handle these cases separately before claiming the workload avoids degeneracy; otherwise the proposed suite can reward unnecessary Horner multiplications rather than representation selection. AGENTS.md explicitly requires adversarial review of exact domains and competent baselines.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Separate algorithm selection from representation selection**

The proposed comparison assigns Horner evaluation to dense/packed storage and indexed exponentiation to sparse storage, then interprets their crossover as a representation-dependent effect. Neither algorithm requires that assignment: a fixed dense or packed representation can scan coefficients and use sparse/gap exponentiation, and sparse storage can use gap-Horner evaluation. Without allowing those conventional controls, the adaptive candidate can win by switching algorithms while the static comparator is artificially restricted, so the 15% hypothesis would not isolate representation-switching utility. Add crossed algorithm/representation controls or explicitly reframe the hypothesis as joint algorithm-and-format selection. AGENTS.md requires competent conventional controls for comparative claims.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Detect host suspension with a suspend-aware clock**

On a Linux host that suspends during the campaign, `CLOCK_MONOTONIC_RAW` stops advancing during suspension, so neither this jump detector nor the deadline measured with the same clock necessarily observes the missing wall time. Guest heartbeats can resume without exposing that interval, allowing a suspended run to receive a success receipt despite the explicit sleep-invalidation requirement. Specify a suspend-aware clock such as `CLOCK_BOOTTIME`, or an independent suspend detector, and make N3 exercise suspension rather than only an artificial forward clock jump.
